speakers.name: Ilya Yuffa
speakers.title: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities

speakers.name: Jake Van Naarden
speakers.title: President, Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development

exchanges.question: How does Lilly see its consumer-facing position expanding, including more aesthetic-driven approaches, and how similar are the US and international self-pay markets?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa: obesity treatment is still at mid-single-digit utilization, access is improving with Bridge and state Medicaid going live or committing next year, obesity TRxs are about 3 million, and about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions are self-pay; Lilly is expanding LillyDirect and consumer awareness. Jonsson: obesity outside the US is still mainly out of pocket, Lilly has launched versions of LillyDirect outside the US, regulations differ so models will differ, and the common aim is reaching patients with safe and authentic Lilly medicines. The aesthetic-driven angle was not addressed.

exchanges.question: Why has the US Foundayo launch curve been slower than anticipated and when will it inflect? Outside the US, what are the competitive dynamics with Novo's oral pill, including share in the UAE where Novo said it reached 50% share within three weeks?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa: three focus areas (physician education, access and affordability, consumer awareness); CVS added Foundayo in June, Bridge launched July 1, full DTC campaign started; in the last week of July volume almost doubled versus a month earlier and about one in four new starts are on Foundayo. Jonsson: UAE launch was early May with a strong start, patients are mostly incretin-naive, Lilly's combined incretin share held steady with a second oral entering, next launches are Mexico and Saudi with most launches in 2027, supply is ready with no gating; the Novo figure is early, noisy sell-in data that includes inventory build.

exchanges.question: What are the requirements and milestones to get retatrutide accepted as a BLA, and would this pathway apply to subsequent incretins?
exchanges.answer: Lilly believes retatrutide is a biologic application (amino acid count rule, analogous to a protein). The first court decision was mixed and litigation is active; Lilly hopes to reach a conclusion with the FDA supporting a BLA. Lilly has the clinical data needed but must gather a little more on CMC, is in communication with the agency, and expects to submit by Q1 next year. The question about subsequent incretins was not addressed.

exchanges.question: What are the learnings and surprises from the Medicare obesity (Bridge) rollout, the ramp curve, and orals versus injectables?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Early days but a significant inflection over the last few weeks for both ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO. Prior authorization and approval process is working well, criteria are clear, and LillyDirect can fulfil Bridge. Roughly 80% of people getting treatment are on injectables, and about 60%-70% are new people who had no prior access.

exchanges.question: Do you need a commercial strategy to protect against retatrutide that is apparently available today, or will formal approval solve that? Does retatrutide's higher efficacy open indications beyond those of tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: On the commercial point, people await authentic retatrutide and will vote with their feet once it is on the market; no specific strategy was described. On development, high-dose weight loss opens more opportunities: knee osteoarthritis pain reduced by 75% (TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1), an ongoing MASH/MASLD study, additional indications under internal evaluation, and a chronic lower back pain study reading out sometime next year.

exchanges.question: What is the post-Verzenio strategy in breast cancer, given the SERD and oral PI3K, and is an all-oral combination on the table?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Lilly believes it has the best medicines for the three key targets (estrogen receptor, CDK4/6, PI3K alpha) and plans to combine them. INLURIYO (imlunestrant) has EMBER-4 in adjuvant reading out next year. The phase III program for tersolisib (PI3K inhibitor) is about to begin, initially with existing endocrine therapies and over time combined with INLURIYO, with investigators' choice of CDK4/6, largely Verzenio. Lilly is excited about an all-oral combination down the road.

exchanges.question: Guidance appears to imply a revenue deceleration in the back half versus Q2 despite Bridge and Foundayo access ramping. Is something missing on price, or is the guide conservative?
exchanges.answer: The guide was upgraded by $2.5 billion. Q2 and recent quarters included one-off prior-period adjustments to US rebate and discount estimates that are not expected to continue in H2. The 2025 base had a bolus of MOUNJARO launches in new countries in H2, which will not repeat, and growth is expected to be more driven by OUS penetration; dollar growth is still expected to be significant. Q3 Europe holiday seasonality and Q4 US Type 2 diabetes seasonality are factored in. He did not say whether the guide is conservative.

exchanges.question: Which regions are driving the strongest OUS growth, and what is being seen in India with generic semaglutide launching and capacity constraints?
exchanges.answer: MOUNJARO is performing very strongly nearly everywhere; China NRDL gave category leadership after 16 months, with significant growth in Korea, the UK, Mexico and Germany, and share in many markets similar to or above the US. In India and Brazil, MOUNJARO TRx continue to grow after generic semaglutide launched, in Canada tirzepatide TRx grow at the pace of the total market, and generic companies face significant supply constraints that Lilly will monitor.

exchanges.question: How extensive is the Foundayo sampling program and is it dampening IQVIA prescription data? Can you quantify the expansion in the US prescriber base?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Lilly is using every promotional lever; sampling covers the first 30 days of the first dose, similar to a typical oral small molecule, extensively across prescribers, with full supply. Prescribers rose from 8,000 at the last earnings call to 36,000 now. He did not address whether sampling depresses IQVIA data.

exchanges.question: Net price per obesity prescription looks well above cash and other benchmarks. How sustainable is that, with medical exceptions and CVS back on formulary, and is it what drives favourable rebate adjustments each quarter?
exchanges.answer: Channel prices are transparent: LillyDirect $299 to $449, Bridge $245, plus commercial. Medical exception and script size are drivers; CVS access, starting in Q4, removes the need for medical exceptions, which he called a short-term thing. He expects price to go down, this is embedded in the guide and reset expectations, and volume growth will more than offset it. No net price figure was given.

exchanges.question: Are psychiatry and vaccines areas Lilly can scale and are they high priority, or are the assets one-offs driven by the science?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Both areas share immense unmet need, which is the through line of internal and BD work; the deals were struck at prices allowing discipline and long-term value creation, and are not that different from other deals this year. He declined to forward look on building more in infectious disease and psychiatry because Lilly will be opportunistic.

exchanges.question: Which one or two pipeline assets outside obesity should the street pay more attention to?
exchanges.answer: Cardiovascular: PCSK9 gene editing and oral and injectable Lp(a) drugs. Neuroscience: psychiatry expansion, sleep-wake disorders with Centessa, and addiction and major depressive disorder possibly addressable with incretin science. Oncology: probably the richest period of readouts ever, including Kelonia in vivo CAR T for multiple myeloma and AJ1-11095. Immunology: progress with the drug (transcript says empagliflozin) and combination ideas in IBD and psoriatic disease. Without incretins the pipeline would still be strong and large.

exchanges.question: UAE Foundayo sales of $31 million were close to half of the $67 million in the US; what is the ex-US obesity potential, and will Foundayo be better reimbursed than tirzepatide for diabetes ex-US?
exchanges.answer: Encouraged by the UAE start but very early days with a lot of noise and an initial inventory build. Most patients are naive to incretins and there is a need for an oral in obesity and Type 2 diabetes; the major OUS rollout and launches happen at the beginning of 2027. Lilly is probably slightly better positioned with an oral for Type 2 reimbursement given three head-to-head trials, but OUS reimbursement takes time and the focus at launch will be chronic weight management.
